content.value_statement: Poor error handling makes failures harder to debug and can break user workflows. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design clear, resilient failure handling patterns.
actual_capabilities: Recommends error handling approaches for Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go.
Explains exception hierarchies, result types, option types, and sentinel errors.
Provides patterns for retries, circuit breakers, error aggregation, and graceful degradation.
Helps improve error messages, cleanup behavior, logging, and failure context.
Supports review of application workflows for missing or weak error handling.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automatic runtime verification.
It does not replace production testing, observability review, or incident analysis.
It must be adapted to each framework, infrastructure, and team standard.
It does not include the referenced extra resource files listed in the playbook.

use_cases.title: Design API Failure Paths
use_cases.description: Create predictable validation, not-found, authorization, and external service error responses for a new API feature.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Debugging
use_cases.description: Review existing error handling and add useful context, logging boundaries, and recovery behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Choose consistent exception, result, retry, and fallback patterns across services and languages.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an error handling pattern for this feature. Explain expected errors, unexpected errors, and the simplest safe implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing code or design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workflow for weak error handling. Identify missing validation, cleanup, logging, retry behavior, and user-facing messages.

prompt_templates.title: Design Resilience
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced service design with external dependencies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design resilient error handling for this service. Include retries, circuit breakers, fallbacks, error wrapping, and observability requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create Team Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a team error handling standard for these languages and services. Include pattern selection rules, examples, review checks, and migration steps.

output_examples.input: A payment service sometimes times out and returns unclear errors to users.
output_examples.output: The response should separate validation failures from provider failures, retry only safe operations, and wrap provider errors with order context.

output_examples.input: A team wants consistent error handling across Python and TypeScript services.
output_examples.output: The guidance would compare exception hierarchies and result types, then define shared naming, logging, and response rules.

output_examples.input: A batch import fails after the first invalid record.
output_examples.output: The recommendation would collect record-level errors, report all actionable failures, and preserve fatal errors for immediate stopping.

best_practices: Define expected failures before choosing exceptions, result types, retries, or fallbacks.
Preserve context without exposing secrets in logs, error messages, or user responses.
Verify behavior with tests for validation, dependency failure, cleanup, and recovery paths.
anti_patterns: Do not catch broad errors without logging, wrapping, rethrowing, or returning a clear result.
Do not retry unsafe operations unless idempotency and side effects are understood.
Do not expose stack traces, internal identifiers, or sensitive details to end users.

faq.question: What languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples and patterns for Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go.

faq.question: Can it fix my code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide changes and review designs, but implementation still depends on your codebase and tests.

faq.question: Does it include retry guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers retry with backoff, circuit breakers, and fallback behavior for external failures.

faq.question: Is it useful for frontend projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns can help with API failures, user messages, async errors, and graceful UI recovery.

faq.question: Does it replace incident review?
faq.answer: No. It supports better design, but incidents still require logs, metrics, traces, and system-specific analysis.

faq.question: How should I start using it?
faq.answer: Start with one workflow, list expected failures, then map each failure to handling, logging, and user response behavior.
